subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw implement native core per-agent spend-budget enforcement, expose only a budget-capable plugin/admission API, or leave budget enforcement to external/provider-account controls?
rationale: The remaining work changes config/default surface, provider dispatch policy, persistent accounting state, and operator UX, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Native core admission layer
options.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets as a core pre-dispatch admission path with durable SQLite accounting, reservations/refunds, receipts, and status/doctor surfaces while allowing plugins to observe or contribute policy.

options.title: Plugin/API-first boundary
options.body: Extend the plugin/admission contract enough for external budget systems to enforce before dispatch and keep OpenClaw core limited to generic hooks and observability.

options.title: External controls only
options.body: Decline native enforcement and document provider accounts, balances, and external proxies as the supported budget-control path.

recommendation.title: Native core admission layer
recommendation.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets as a core pre-dispatch admission path with durable SQLite accounting, reservations/refunds, receipts, and status/doctor surfaces while allowing plugins to observe or contribute policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed connection to adjacent runaway-runtime guardrails and core product boundary decisions, though implementation ownership is shared.
